desc: Wispy, feathery ice crystal clouds. Fair weather indicator. Form above 6 km. Thin, white, hair-like streaks. Latin for "curl" or "wisp of hair".

desc: Fluffy, cotton-like clouds with flat bases. Form by convection. Fair weather cumulus (humilis) or towering (congestus). Base typically 1 km.

desc: Uniform gray sheet covering entire sky. Drizzle or snow possible. Fog lifted off ground. Diffuse light. Low overcast layer.

desc: Thunderstorm cloud. Towering, dense, anvil-shaped top. Produces rain, lightning, hail, tornadoes. Can reach tropopause (16 km). Most powerful cloud type.

desc: Dark gray rain cloud. Continuous steady precipitation. Thick layer blotting out sun. Extensive horizontal coverage.

desc: Grayish/bluish uniform layer. Sun visible as through frosted glass. Often precedes warm front. Thin enough for faint shadows.

desc: Transparent whitish veil covering sky. Creates halos around sun/moon. Ice crystal composition. Signals approaching warm front.
